messages.author: e14cfb57d640984d
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Very long time of computation with certain files
parts:
HI Daniel,

There are lots of reasons why calculations could take a long time, but one way to speed up the H() or specprop() calculations would be to use a larger spectrogram window length (parameter wl). You would give this parameter directly to the H() function, or use it to create the underlying spec objects which you're passing to specprop().

The default wl is 512. Depending on what you're interested in in these sound files, you might be able to use a significantly larger window. For instance, for certain bird vocalizations without a lot of fast frequency modulation, you could potentially get away with a wl as high as 2048 at your sampling rate of 44 kHz (theoretically cutting computation time by a factor of four). Perhaps a good rule of thumb would be to use a wl that allows you to see details of interest when you display a signal of interest with spectro().

best,
jesse
